A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same cMG/TRPE research, despite the changed title and organization. The complete main texts, figures, equations, and appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 6 and Appendix C report original entropy-maximization, policy-pretraining, and downstream-return experiments in Secret Room and two-agent Reacher.

after.justification: Section 6 and Appendix C retain these original experimental results, including sparse-reward learning and zero-shot evaluation.

M1.justification: The three objective formulations and TRPE procedure are retained. Per-agent importance sampling, the surrogate objective, and KL-constrained gradient updates are unchanged; v4 expands their explanation.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Secret Room and two-agent MaMuJoCo Reacher for reward-free exploration and downstream tasks. The new search-and-rescue example in Appendix A is illustrative, not an additional evaluated task.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same joint, disjoint, and mixture objective variants and uniform/random-initialization controls. Newly cited methods do not become evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Section 6 and Appendix C retain the exploration horizons, 10-bin discretization, goal conditions, reward definitions, training budgets, network configurations, and entropy/return metrics. Added explanatory passages do not revise the reported settings.

E4.justification: The longer-horizon, per-agent state-entropy, and policy-entropy analyses in v3 Figures 3–4 remain in v4 Figures 4–5. New Appendix A provides conceptual discussion, not additional empirical analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions specify four seeds and report averages with 95% confidence intervals in the corresponding main experimental figures. The new checklist reiterates this practice without adding statistical procedures.

E6.justification: The empirical graphics in v3 Figures 1–4 are retained as v4 Figures 2–5, with matching curves, bars, visitation maps, and uncertainty displays. No experimental result entries or reported performance findings are added or removed.

T1.justification: The objective definitions, Lemma 4.1, Theorem 4.2, convergence result, and Appendix B proofs are retained. The Lipschitz assumption moves from Appendix B to Section 2; notation changes and added Bellman-operator discussion do not introduce new formal results or derivations.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain the three entropy formulations, their theoretical characterization, TRPE, and mixture-based pretraining benefits for coordination and downstream performance. The revised title and contribution outline restate this scientific scope.

C2.justification: Remark 1 and new Appendix A qualify when mixture entropy is appropriate, explaining its treatment of agent permutations and when joint-state coverage is preferable. Section 6 adds emphasis on downstream return and elaborates disjoint-policy overfitting. Existing TRPE estimator limitations are relocated rather than newly introduced.

D1.justification: Appendix C retains the implementation details, hyperparameters, Apple M2 hardware, memory and execution-time information, and identical code-repository link. The new checklist repeats existing reproducibility disclosures.

R1.justification: v4 substantially broadens the literature coverage and positioning, including zero-sum cMGs, state-entropy-regularized MDPs, additional exploration methods, and zero-shot RL. New connections include Kalogiannis et al. (2025), Brekelmans et al. (2022), Ashlag et al. (2025), and Zisselman et al. (2023); these extend the discussion beyond the relocated v3 related-work text.

P1.justification: v4 retitles the paper, systematically adopts state-entropy-maximization terminology, adds a substantial contribution outline, and expands several explanations. Related work moves into the main text, assumptions and limitations are relocated, and a new objective-discussion appendix and NeurIPS checklist substantially reorganize the document.

P2.justification: v4 adds an explanatory distribution diagram as Figure 1 and shaded research-question boxes, and reformats the author block and algorithm presentation. Existing empirical figures retain their panel structures and graphics while being renumbered and reflowed.

improvement.justification: The new distribution diagram, clearer contribution outline, and expanded research context make the retained framework easier to understand. Remark 1 and Appendix A also provide useful qualifications about choosing mixture versus joint entropy. These improve clarity and applicability discussion while leaving the underlying experimental evidence and formal results unchanged.
